Praha-Troja — Prague, Czechia

Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Praha-Troja is one of Prague's 57 official mestske casti (city districts). Policie CR (the Czech national police) recorded 362 incidents here in 2024 across a population of 1,603 residents — a rate of 22,583 incidents per 100,000 residents, roughly 1.7× the citywide district average. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central/tourist district can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential district can show a low rate simply by having few incidents relative to its population. This district has a small population (1,603 residents), so its rate per 100,000 residents can swing sharply from a handful of cases and should be read with that in mind rather than as a stable per-visit risk measure. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Prague — real Policie CR incident data and real CSU population figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Praha-Troja safe?

Wandroz currently rates Praha-Troja in Prague, Czechia as an area where Wandroz's data suggests extra caution relative to other areas covered during the day and an area where Wandroz's data suggests extra caution relative to other areas covered at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

Is Praha-Troja safe at night?

At night, Praha-Troja is rated as an area where Wandroz's data suggests extra caution relative to other areas covered. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Praha-Troja a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Praha-Troja's day rating (an area where Wandroz's data suggests extra caution relative to other areas covered) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. Is there official crime data for Praha-Troja?

Not yet at neighbourhood level. Unlike London, this city does not currently publish an open, geolocated crime dataset at this level of detail (checked against the relevant local and national open-data portals — see the methodology page for what was checked).
